key_insight: Turbulent energy dissipation is not uniform but multifractal, meaning its intermittency is organized across scales by multiplicative cascade-like processes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a statistical framework for predicting extreme dissipation events that matter in turbulence modeling, mixing, combustion, and high-resolution CFD.
method: Interpreted point-probe dissipation measurements using multifractal formalism and cascade-model theory.
Applied Taylor’s frozen-flow hypothesis to convert time signals into spatial statistics in laboratory and atmospheric flows.
Estimated the multifractal spectrum f(α) with multiple averaging methods and compared it against cascade models.
evidence_signal: Experiments across several laboratory flows and the atmospheric surface layer showed consistent f(α) spectra, with long data sets also revealing the latent part of the spectrum and square-root exponential dissipation tails.
watch_item: Results rely on Taylor’s frozen-flow hypothesis and point measurements, so strong shear, nonstationarity, or insufficient record length can bias inferred multifractal spectra.
paper_title: The multifractal nature of turbulent energy dissipation
